name: ls
description: List files and directories in the current directory or a path you specify.

examples.explanation: Display a detailed listing with permissions, ownership, size, and modification time.
Include hidden files and directories such as .bashrc

name: pwd
description: Print the path of your current working directory.

examples.explanation: Shows the current working directory.
Show the directory and it's path

name: cd
description: Move the shell into a different working directory.

examples.explanation: Move up to the parent directory.
Go to your home directory.

name: mkdir
description: Create a directory or a hierarchy of directories.

examples.explanation: Create a directory named Projects.
Creates parent directory Projects and it's nested children.

name: cp
description: Copy a file, or recursively copy a directory and its contents.

examples.explanation: Copy notes.txt to backup.txt.
Copy Projects and its contents into ProjectsBackup. -r is a recursive flag.

name: mv
description: Move files and directories to a new location, or give them a new name.

examples.explanation: Renames draft.txt to final.txt.
Move the file into an existing Documents directory.

name: rm
description: Remove a file or, with the recursive option, a directory tree.

examples.explanation: Removes draft.txt.
Recursively remove the Projects directory and its contents.

name: find
description: Search a directory tree for files and directories that match conditions.

examples.explanation: Find names ending in .txt under the current directory. * is a wildcard.
List directories under the current directory, including the starting directory.

name: cat
description: Write the contents of one or more files to standard output.

examples.explanation: Display the contents of notes.txt.
Display the file with numbered lines.

name: less
summary: Read text one screen at a time
description: Browse a text file interactively without editing it.

examples.explanation: Open notes.txt for reading.
Show line numbers while browsing.

name: grep
description: Print lines that match a text pattern.

examples.explanation: Show lines containing the lowercase text error.
Ignore letter case and include line numbers.

name: head
summary: Read the start of a file
description: Display the first lines of a text file.

examples.explanation: Show the first 10 lines.
Show the first 5 lines.

name: tail
summary: Read the end of a file
description: Display the last lines of a file or watch new content as it is appended.

examples.explanation: Show the last 5 lines.
displays the most recent lines added, as they appear.

name: sort
description: Sort lines from a file or standard input.

examples.explanation: Sort files alphabetically.
Sorts values numerically instead of as text.

name: chmod
description: Change the read, write, and execute permissions on a file or directory.

examples.explanation: Add execute permission for the file owner.
Allow the owner to read/write, the group to read, and others no access.

name: whoami
description: Print the username associated with your effective user ID.

examples.explanation: Display the effective username of the current process.
Use id to display the effective username as an alternative.

name: id
description: Display user and group identity information.

examples.explanation: Show your user ID, primary group, and group memberships.
Show your group names.

name: ps
description: Display a snapshot of processes and their information.

examples.explanation: Show the default selection of processes associated with your user and terminal.
Show all processes in a full-format listing on Linux.

name: top
description: Display a regularly updated overview of processes and system resource use.

examples.explanation: Open the interactive process monitor.
Show processes belonging to your current username.

name: kill
summary: Send a signal to a process
description: Send a signal to a process identified by its process ID.

examples.explanation: Request termination of process 1234.
List signal names available in your implementation.
